verses.1: Elders among you, therefore, I appeal as a fellow elder and as a witness of the sufferings of the Messiah, and as one who will share in the glory that is going to be revealed,
verses.2: shepherd the flock of God in your midst, keeping watch over them not under compulsion, but willingly, as God wills; nor as seeking to gain from them, but eagerly,
verses.3: nor as lording it over those assigned to you, but being an example to the flock.
verses.4: And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive the imperishable crown of glory.
verses.5: Likewise, younger ones, submit yourselves to the elders. All of you clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, for God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
verses.6: Therefore, humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time,
verses.7: casting all your anxieties on Him, because He cares for you.
verses.8: Be alert, be self-controlled. Your adversary the devil is prowling like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
verses.9: Resist him, standing firm in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being fulfilled in your brothers who are in the world.
verses.10: The God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little while, will Himself perfect, strengthen, establish, and support you.
verses.11: To Him be the power forever and ever. Amen.
verses.12: Through Silvanus, I wrote to you, whom I consider faithful, with just a few words, exhorting and testifying that this grace of God is true; stand in it.
verses.13: Greetings to you from the chosen ones in Babylon, and from my son Mark.
verses.14: Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "the chosen ones in Babylon" — the reference to "Babylon" is likely symbolic or metaphorical, though some interpret it as literal. The term "chosen ones" reflects συνεκλεκτὴ (syneklektē), meaning "fellow-chosen."

[2] shepherd the flock of God in your midst, keeping watch over them not under compulsion, but willingly, as God wills; nor as seeking to gain from them, but eagerly,

[6] Therefore, humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time, 
[7] casting all your anxieties on Him, because He cares for you. 
[8] Be alert, be self-controlled. Your adversary the devil is prowling like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. 
[9] Resist him, standing firm in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being fulfilled in your brothers who are in the world.
